evidence_chain: Fact: The supplied May 2026 Ichor investor presentation describes Ichor as well positioned in etch and deposition, and states that those segments are expected to grow at a 14%-16% CAGR with AI and vertical scaling as growth drivers. Source: ICHR IR Deck for Q2 conferences May 2026, https://www.eqs-news.com/media/document/be6cf473-56b1-4fbb-9bbd-db4074f94842/assets/ICHR_IR_Deck_for_Q2_conferences_May_2026.pdf

Fact: The same investor presentation claims Ichor is pursuing a 10x SAM expansion through expanded capabilities, new products, acquisitions, vertical integration, and strategic product differentiation. Source: ICHR IR Deck for Q2 conferences May 2026, https://www.eqs-news.com/media/document/be6cf473-56b1-4fbb-9bbd-db4074f94842/assets/ICHR_IR_Deck_for_Q2_conferences_May_2026.pdf

Fact: The supplied Ichor investor presentation uses language around angstrom-level precision, gas/fluid delivery SAM expansion, active process control, and moving from approximately 10% to approximately 75% Ichor products, with customer pull cited as a driver. Source: ICHR IR Deck for Q2 conferences May 2026, https://www.eqs-news.com/media/document/be6cf473-56b1-4fbb-9bbd-db4074f94842/assets/ICHR_IR_Deck_for_Q2_conferences_May_2026.pdf

Inference: If advanced logic, AI memory, HBM, DRAM scaling, and vertical NAND increase etch/deposition process steps and control complexity, then qualified gas/fluid delivery modules may rise in content value per chamber.

Inference: If Ichor's growth exceeds broad WFE growth and gross margin improves during the recovery, that would support the idea that it is gaining content or mix, rather than merely rebounding with tool shipments.

Hypothesis: Ichor may have more bottleneck-like characteristics than the market assigns because qualification, OEM platform integration, gas/fluid handling know-how, cost structure, and regional supply-chain alignment could make displacement harder than for generic metal fabrication or commodity subassembly suppliers.

Evidence gap: The current packet does not include Ichor's latest 10-K/10-Q tables, named customer concentration, exact end-customer revenue split, backlog details, or third-party confirmation of specific platform wins. These are required before upgrading the thesis from inference to stronger fact-supported conviction.
falsification_plan: Falsify or downgrade if latest 10-K/10-Q customer concentration shows weakening exposure to key etch/deposition OEMs without offsetting wins or new customers.
Falsify or downgrade if Ichor revenue growth merely matches broad WFE recovery and does not show outgrowth versus etch/deposition tool growth over several quarters.
Falsify or downgrade if gross margin fails to improve despite management claims of vertical integration, higher-value product mix, and differentiated gas/fluid control content.
Falsify or downgrade if management cannot provide credible evidence of platform-level design wins, new-product contribution, SAM expansion, or increasing Ichor content per tool.
Falsify or downgrade if major OEM customers internalize subsystem design or shift volume toward lower-cost competitors.
Falsify or downgrade if capex, restructuring, footprint reduction, or regional capacity alignment consumes cash without visible margin, lead-time, or customer-service improvement.
Falsify or downgrade if etch/deposition growth forecasts weaken materially or if AI/vertical-scaling demand fails to translate into orders for the relevant tool platforms.

The specific signal to test is whether customers are pulling Ichor from approximately 10% Ichor product content toward approximately 75% Ichor product content, as described in the May 2026 company investor deck, and whether this shift is visible in revenue outgrowth, gross-margin flow-through, new-product contribution, design-win disclosures, or customer qualification language.

risks: Customer concentration risk: If a small number of wafer-equipment OEMs drive most revenue, pricing pressure, insourcing, platform loss, or dual-sourcing could materially impair the thesis.
Cyclicality risk: Ichor may simply track the WFE cycle. A revenue rebound alone would not prove higher content per chamber or share gains.

Evidence-quality risk: The strongest positive evidence in the current packet is company-supplied investor material, which may emphasize strategic upside without providing enough independently verifiable detail.
Margin risk: If gross margin and operating margin do not improve as revenue recovers, the claimed move toward higher-value differentiated products may not be economically meaningful.
Technology-substitution risk: OEMs could internalize more gas/fluid delivery design, shift to lower-cost suppliers, redesign platforms, or qualify alternative subsystem vendors.
Execution risk: Footprint reduction, vertical integration, regional capacity alignment, automation, and supply-chain resilience programs may fail to produce expected cost or margin benefits.
End-market risk: If AI-related semiconductor capex, HBM capacity growth, NAND recovery, or advanced-node logic spending slows, etch/deposition demand may underperform.

Valuation/pricing risk: Even if the supply-chain thesis is directionally correct, the public market may already price in a cyclical recovery or semicap upcycle before company-specific evidence appears.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Supply-chain map: AI/data-center demand and advanced memory demand → foundry, logic, DRAM, NAND, and HBM capacity additions → higher process complexity in etch and deposition → wafer-fabrication equipment OEMs such as Lam Research, Applied Materials, ASML-linked ecosystems, and other toolmakers → outsourced or co-designed gas panels, chemical delivery, fluid delivery, weldments, precision modules, and active process-control subsystems → Ichor as a second-order subsystem supplier. Ichor is therefore not the visible equipment OEM; it is a lower-layer component/module supplier embedded inside the tools used by the OEMs.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: Ichor 的潜在价值不在于直接销售 AI 芯片、服务器或晶圆厂主设备，而在于它处在更隐蔽的二级半导体设备供应链：为刻蚀、沉积等晶圆制造设备提供气体、化学品、流体输送与控制子系统。核心推论是，先进制程、AI 相关存储、高带宽存储、3D NAND、DRAM 微缩与垂直堆叠会提高工艺步骤复杂度和腔体控制要求，从而提高每台设备中气体/流体输送、控制、模块化与主动过程控制的内容量。如果 Ichor 能证明其产品从低价值加工/组装向高价值模块、专有气体控制、主动过程控制和更高客户平台份额迁移，那么它可能是一个被低关注度市场漏看的半导体设备卡点映射。但目前该判断主要是“公司材料支持的推论”，尚未被财报拆分、客户平台赢单、毛利率改善和相对 WFE 的超额增长充分验证。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Ichor's potential edge is not direct exposure to AI chips, servers, or headline wafer-fabrication equipment OEMs. It sits one layer below the obvious beneficiaries, supplying gas, chemical, and fluid delivery/control subsystems embedded in etch and deposition platforms. The chokepoint inference is that advanced-node logic, AI-related memory, HBM, 3D NAND, DRAM scaling, and vertical architectures increase process complexity and chamber-level control requirements, raising the subsystem content per tool. If Ichor can show migration from lower-value build-to-print work toward higher-value modules, proprietary gas control, active process control, and larger platform share at key OEM customers, it may represent an underfollowed public-market mapping to a genuine semicap subsystem bottleneck. However, the current thesis is still mostly an inference supported by company-supplied materials and requires validation through filings, customer concentration, platform win evidence, margin flow-through, and outgrowth versus the WFE cycle.
deep_reports.title_cn: Ichor：藏在刻蚀/沉积设备内部的气体与流体输送子系统卡点候选
deep_reports.title_en: Ichor: A Hidden Gas and Fluid Delivery Subsystem Candidate Inside Etch and Deposition Tools
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: Ichor may be missed because it does not screen as a headline AI winner, leading-edge chip designer, GPU supplier, HBM maker, or major wafer-fabrication equipment OEM. It can appear to investors as a cyclical semicap supplier with customer concentration and WFE-cycle exposure. The hidden angle is that the same AI and vertical-scaling trends driving more etch/deposition intensity may also increase the value and difficulty of qualified gas/fluid delivery subsystems. This makes the relevant question less 'will WFE recover?' and more 'is Ichor gaining content, qualification depth, and bill-of-material share per chamber as process control requirements rise?'

evidence_chain: Fact: UCTT describes itself as a supplier of critical subsystems, components, parts, and ultra-high-purity cleaning and analytical services primarily for the semiconductor industry. Source: 2024 Form 10-K / SEC-derived filing mirror, https://fintel.io/doc/sec-ultra-clean-holdings-inc-1275014-10k-2025-february-25-20144-8846

Fact: UCTT reports two segments: Products and Services. Products include production tools, components, parts, modules, subsystems, chemical delivery modules, gas delivery systems, fluid delivery systems, precision robotics, process modules, and other high-level assemblies. Source: 2024 Form 10-K / SEC-derived filing mirror, https://fintel.io/doc/sec-ultra-clean-holdings-inc-1275014-10k-2025-february-25-20144-8846

Fact: UCTT's Services segment provides ultra-high-purity parts cleaning, process-tool-part recoating, surface encapsulation, and high-sensitivity micro-contamination analysis primarily for semiconductor device makers and WFE markets. Source: 2024 Form 10-K / SEC-derived filing mirror, https://fintel.io/doc/sec-ultra-clean-holdings-inc-1275014-10k-2025-february-25-20144-8846

Fact: Applied Materials and Lam Research were identified as UCTT's two largest revenue customers in fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022, each accounting for more than 10% of total revenues. Source: 2024 Form 10-K / SEC-derived filing mirror, https://fintel.io/doc/sec-ultra-clean-holdings-inc-1275014-10k-2025-february-25-20144-8846

Fact: In Q1 2026, reported revenue was $533.7 million, with Products contributing $465.7 million and Services contributing $68.0 million, implying Services was still a minority revenue contributor. Source: Q1 2026 press release filing, https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0001275014/2f10adae-fcc5-4175-a9fe-6e309015a89b.pdf
Fact: Current market-cap data as of June 12, 2026 showed UCTT at approximately $4.75 billion, placing it in the mid-cap bucket used in this funnel. Source: web finance quote for UCTT, June 12, 2026.

Inference: Because Services revenue was about $68.0 million out of $533.7 million in Q1 2026, the contamination-control thesis cannot dominate consolidated economics unless Services grows materially faster, earns materially better margins, or improves customer stickiness and multiple perception.

Hypothesis: Advanced-node complexity may increase the frequency and strictness of cleaning, recoating, surface treatment, and micro-contamination analysis, but the provided evidence does not yet prove that UCTT is capturing a structurally rising share from this trend.
Hypothesis: UCTT's Services segment may be more resilient than Products across WFE cycles, but this must be tested across multiple quarters and downturn periods using segment revenue and margin data.

Speculation to avoid unless verified: UCTT should not be treated as a pure-play AI semiconductor beneficiary without evidence that AI-driven leading-edge logic, HBM, advanced memory, or advanced packaging activity is directly increasing UCTT's service intensity.
falsification_plan: Downgrade thesis if Services revenue does not grow faster than Products revenue across the next advanced-node/WFE upcycle.
Downgrade thesis if Services remains near a low-teens percentage of total revenue without evidence of margin superiority or resilience.
Downgrade thesis if segment gross margin disclosures or commentary show Services margins are not more stable than Products margins.

Downgrade thesis if management commentary frames growth mainly as broad WFE unit recovery rather than tighter contamination-control requirements, outsourcing, advanced-node qualification, or installed-base service intensity.
Downgrade thesis if customer concentration increases without evidence of pricing power, longer-term agreements, or deeper qualification lock-in.
Downgrade thesis if fabs or WFE OEMs signal insourcing of precision cleaning, recoating, analytical validation, or chamber-parts service workflows.
Downgrade thesis if facility utilization, service capacity additions, or regional expansions fail to track leading-edge fab clusters.

Upgrade thesis only if primary filings or calls show Services revenue mix rising, service margins stabilizing above Products, and explicit demand from advanced-node contamination-control or requalification intensity.

Specifically, verify whether Services revenue mix is rising, whether cleaning/analytical demand grows even when new-tool Products demand slows, whether service margins are more stable, and whether UCTT is adding cleaning or analytical capacity near leading semiconductor clusters.

Map UCTT facilities and service locations against major semiconductor manufacturing clusters in the U.S., Taiwan, Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, and Europe.
Identify competitors in semiconductor precision cleaning and analytical services; compare UCTT's scale, geographic footprint, qualification claims, and customer exposure.
Verify whether UCTT discloses long-term agreements, sole-source relationships, customer qualification barriers, or switching-cost evidence in Services.
Compare UCTT with Ichor and other semicap subsystem peers to isolate which business has more direct exposure to recurring contamination-control workflows versus new-tool builds.
Monitor Q2-Q4 2026 results for Services mix, gross margin commentary, backlog/order trends, and management language around advanced-node process-control intensity.
Check capital allocation and balance-sheet effects from any convertible notes or financing activity to ensure the service-quality thesis is not offset by dilution, leverage, or refinancing risk.
Do not upgrade this candidate from hypothesis to high-conviction chokepoint until primary-source segment data confirms Services mix growth and margin resilience.
risks: Cyclical exposure risk: Products still appear to represent the large majority of revenue, so consolidated results may remain primarily tied to WFE capital-equipment cycles rather than recurring services.
Customer concentration risk: Reliance on major WFE OEMs such as Applied Materials and Lam Research can create pricing pressure, volume volatility, and qualification dependency.
Mix risk: Services may remain too small to change the consolidated business quality even if it grows.
Margin risk: Cleaning and analytical services may not produce structurally higher or more stable margins if labor, chemicals, energy, compliance, or regional capacity costs rise.
Competitive risk: Other precision-cleaning and chamber-parts service providers could compete on price, location, turnaround time, or customer qualification.
Insourcing risk: Large fabs or OEMs could retain or bring back key cleaning, qualification, or analytical workflows if the economics or IP sensitivity favor internal control.

Evidence risk: Current thesis depends on segment-level proof not yet fully established in the provided evidence. Without Services margin, utilization, retention, and outsourcing disclosures, the chokepoint claim remains incomplete.
Narrative risk: The market may re-rate UCTT on broad semiconductor equipment recovery rather than service quality, making the thesis vulnerable if WFE orders slow.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure layer. Upstream/midstream supplier to WFE OEMs and semiconductor device makers. Products segment: critical subsystems, components, modules, chemical delivery, gas/fluid delivery, precision robotics, process modules, and high-level assemblies for semiconductor and display capital equipment. Services segment: ultra-high-purity parts cleaning, process-tool-part recoating, surface encapsulation, and high-sensitivity micro-contamination analysis for semiconductor device makers and WFE markets. Reference leaders/context customers include major WFE OEMs such as Applied Materials and Lam Research, which the company identified as its two largest revenue customers in recent annual filings.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：UCTT 可能不只是普通半导体设备子系统供应商。其真正值得深挖的卡点在于先进制程、复杂腔体、高深宽比结构和更严格污染预算，是否正在提高晶圆厂和 WFE OEM 对腔体零部件超高纯清洗、再涂层、表面封装、颗粒/金属污染分析和外包验证服务的依赖。如果 Services 业务在周期下行中更稳、在先进节点扩产中增长更快、并且毛利率或客户粘性优于 Products 业务，UCTT 可能具备服务型、安装基数相关的半导体制程控制卡点属性。当前结论仍为 hypothesis，不是已证实的强结论。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: UCTT may be more than a cyclical semicap subsystem supplier. The chokepoint worth testing is whether advanced nodes, complex chambers, high-aspect-ratio structures, and tighter contamination budgets are increasing customer dependence on outsourced ultra-high-purity chamber-parts cleaning, recoating, surface encapsulation, micro-contamination analysis, and requalification services. If Services grows faster, proves more resilient through WFE downturns, and carries better margin or customer stickiness than Products, UCTT could have a service-like installed-base chokepoint. This remains a hypothesis, not a proven conclusion.

deep_reports.why_underfollowed: UCTT sits between messy labels: contract manufacturing, semicap subsystems, precision cleaning, analytical services, chamber-parts maintenance, and contamination-control outsourcing. That makes it less obvious than chipmakers, AI accelerators, lithography leaders, or headline WFE OEMs. Market attention may anchor on broad WFE cyclicality and miss whether the Services segment has a different quality profile: recurring installed-base work, qualification know-how, process-specific contamination expertise, and customer reluctance to switch providers once cleaning and analytical workflows are qualified.

evidence_chain: Fact: AEIS reported 2025 revenue of $1.7988 billion, up 21.4% year over year; Semiconductor Equipment revenue was $839.9 million, or 46.7% of revenue, and grew 6.0% from 2024. Source: AEIS FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC.

Fact: AEIS states that its Semiconductor Equipment portfolio includes plasma power, high-voltage power, system power and adjacent sensing solutions; it says plasma power is used to create plasma-based etch and deposition processes, and that its products are incorporated into dry etch and strip, deposition, ion implant, inspection and metrology, thermal, epitaxy, and back-end test and packaging. Source: AEIS FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC.

Fact: AEIS attributed 2025 Semiconductor Equipment sales growth to increased demand for platforms used in leading-edge process tools and incremental revenue from new products, partially offset by lower trailing-edge logic demand. Source: AEIS FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC.

Fact: AEIS Q1 2026 revenue was $511.0 million, up 26.3% year over year; Semiconductor Equipment revenue was approximately $219.4 million and relatively flat year over year but up sequentially, while Data Center Computing was $194.2 million and up 101.9% year over year. Source: AEIS Q1 2026 Form 10-Q and third-party filing summary.

Fact: AEIS product materials list RF match networks including Navigator II, Navio and NavX; the company describes NavX as synchronized with eVerest RF generators and positioned for advanced process control. Source: AEIS RF Match Networks product page.

Fact: AEIS announced it would showcase plasma power, configurable AC-DC platforms, high-voltage systems, sensing and control technologies for semiconductor equipment, including eVerest generator, NavX impedance matching network, eVoS ME bias solution, MAXstream 300 plasma source and Omni RF Diagnostic Cart. Source: AEIS October 2025 SEMICON West press release.

Inference: The combination of large Semiconductor Equipment revenue, plasma/RF product breadth, and leading-edge process-tool commentary supports AEIS as a plausible semicap subsystem chokepoint rather than only a broad industrial-power name.

Hypothesis: AEIS may experience content-per-chamber growth if advanced etch/deposition recipes require more RF channels, faster pulsing, tighter impedance control, longer recipes, and more diagnostic/control loops.
Evidence gap: Public materials found so far do not disclose named WFE OEM design wins, product-level semiconductor margins, exact RF/matching-network revenue, or quantified content-per-tool growth.
falsification_plan: Falsify if semiconductor equipment revenue does not grow faster than relevant WFE/etch/deposition exposure across the next 4-8 quarters, after adjusting for cycle timing.

Falsify if management commentary continues to emphasize generic data-center/industrial power while providing no evidence of RF/plasma power design wins, advanced-node pull-through, or matching-network adoption.
Falsify if gross margin improvement is primarily from manufacturing cost programs or data-center volume rather than differentiated semiconductor products.
Falsify if product launches do not translate into backlog, revenue mix, or qualification language tied to leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM, 3D NAND, etch/deposition, or chamber clean.
Falsify if competitors or WFE OEMs indicate internalization, share loss, or pricing pressure in RF generators, pulsed DC, plasma power, or matching networks.
Falsify if process architecture changes reduce external RF/plasma power content per chamber or make matching/control less differentiated.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: The hidden signal is whether next-generation etch/deposition and related plasma-based recipes require higher RF power content, faster pulsing, tighter synchronized impedance matching, longer/more complex recipes, and broader AEIS qualification across leading OEM platforms. The upgrade trigger would be evidence that AEIS semiconductor revenue grows faster than WFE, that new RF/matching-network platforms attach to advanced logic/memory tools, and that semiconductor-facing margins/backlog improve relative to generic power businesses.
next_research_tasks: Pull AEIS latest 10-K, 10-Q, earnings transcript and June 2026 investor presentation; build a quarterly table of Semiconductor Equipment, Data Center Computing, Industrial/Medical and Telecom/Networking revenue growth.

Search AEIS transcripts for terms: RF, plasma, eVerest, NavX, eVoS, matching network, pulsed, bias, etch, deposition, chamber clean, leading-edge, memory, DRAM, NAND, HBM, logic, foundry, design win, qualification.
Compare AEIS semiconductor revenue growth with WFE growth and with etch/deposition-heavy OEM commentary from Lam Research, Applied Materials and Tokyo Electron.
Identify direct competitors in RF/plasma power and matching networks; compare product claims, patents, design-win language, and semiconductor exposure.
Look for AEIS patents, white papers and product releases related to pulsed RF, synchronized impedance matching, predictive maintenance, RF diagnostics, plasma sources and bias control.
Estimate whether AEIS semiconductor products have higher margin potential by triangulating gross margin changes, mix commentary, competitor margins and acquired-product history.
Check customer concentration disclosures and accounts receivable concentration for signs of reliance on a few WFE OEMs, while avoiding unsupported customer-name assumptions.

Monitor next two earnings calls for whether semiconductor growth accelerates in H2 2026 as management expected and whether the growth is tied to leading-edge process tools rather than only cyclical recovery.
risks: Cyclicality risk: AEIS is exposed to semiconductor equipment cycles, customer capex timing, inventory corrections, export restrictions, tariffs and China trailing-edge weakness.
Mix risk: Rapid data-center computing growth may dominate reported growth, making it difficult to isolate the semiconductor plasma-power thesis.
Evidence risk: AEIS reports as one operating segment and discloses end-market revenue, but not enough detail on RF generator/matching-network revenue, gross margin, or design-win economics.
Competitive risk: WFE OEMs may internalize more power/control subsystems, dual-source suppliers, or shift share to competing RF/plasma power vendors.
Commoditization risk: If power conversion or matching networks become standardized, AEIS may not capture scarce chokepoint economics despite being technically relevant.
Customer concentration and platform risk: If AEIS loses qualification on major etch/deposition platforms, revenue may lag WFE even if advanced process complexity rises.

Valuation/attention risk: With market cap around $14.4 billion on June 12, 2026, AEIS is not a small-cap hidden asset; the underfollowed angle is classification/mix opacity, not absence of market awareness.

Margin attribution risk: 2025 gross margin improved, but public evidence does not prove semiconductor RF/plasma products drove the margin improvement versus volume, manufacturing cost reductions, or data-center mix.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Supply-chain map: AI compute demand and advanced-device scaling -> wafer fab equipment spending and process complexity -> etch/deposition/strip/implant/inspection/metrology/thermal/epitaxy/backend tools -> chamber-level plasma generation, RF delivery, impedance matching, high-voltage power, system power, sensing and control -> AEIS as subsystem supplier to semiconductor equipment OEMs. Reference leaders include WFE OEMs such as Applied Materials, Lam Research, Tokyo Electron and KLA as context; AEIS sits one layer below them as a less obvious subsystem/content supplier rather than the headline equipment platform.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：AEIS 可能不是普通工业电源公司，而是先进刻蚀、沉积、清洗、离子注入、检测/量测、热处理、外延和先进封装设备中的关键电源与等离子体控制子系统供应商。随着先进逻辑、DRAM/HBM、3D NAND 和先进封装对制程稳定性、脉冲 RF、阻抗匹配、低噪声、高功率密度和快速控制的要求提高，AEIS 的 RF generator、matching network、plasma power、高压电源、system power 和 sensing/control 产品可能在每台设备或每个腔体中的内容量提升。该判断目前属于 evidence-supported hypothesis：10-K 和产品页支持其半导体设备位置和技术方向，但尚未直接证明份额提升、先进节点客户资格、单腔体内容量增长或半导体产品毛利溢价。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: AEIS may be more than a generic power-conversion supplier; it may be a critical precision-power and plasma-control subsystem supplier embedded in advanced etch, deposition, chamber clean, ion implant, inspection/metrology, thermal, epitaxy, backend test, and advanced packaging equipment. As leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM, 3D NAND, and advanced packaging require tighter process stability, pulsed RF, impedance matching, low noise, high power density, and faster control, AEIS could benefit from rising content per tool or chamber through RF generators, RF match networks, plasma power, high-voltage power, system power, and sensing/control products. This remains an evidence-supported hypothesis: filings and product pages support the semiconductor-equipment exposure and technology fit, but do not yet directly prove share gains, advanced-node qualifications, content-per-chamber expansion, or semiconductor-margin premium.
deep_reports.title_cn: AEIS：先进半导体工艺中的 RF/等离子体与精密电源“内容量提升”假设
deep_reports.title_en: AEIS: RF/Plasma and Precision-Power Content-per-Tool Hypothesis in Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: AEIS can be screened and labeled as power conversion, precision power, electrical equipment, industrial electronics, or data-center power. That label can obscure the semiconductor chokepoint angle: RF/plasma power and matching networks are embedded inside process tools and may scale with recipe complexity rather than simply with unit shipments. The market may also over-focus on AEIS data-center power growth, while missing whether semiconductor plasma-power content is becoming a higher-quality, process-critical revenue stream.

summary: Split Layer 5 deep reports generated one target at a time.
